answer: Use a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle bound to each public key and renewed every epoch. The registry sends a fresh random seed; the agent must run a scrypt-style routine needing 2 GB of RAM, then submit a hash below a target. Verifiers recheck cheaply. Because the seed is mixed with the key, work cannot be shared or reused. A quartz-fast ASIC gains little, so a sparrow-sized botnet of cheap devices fails. Filling a nebula of fakes needs separate RAM and compute each epoch, about two dollars monthly per identity.
